historical_references.reference: The name Ashmit is a Sanskrit word meaning 'pain, suffering or torment'. It is also found in Indian mythology as the name of a demon king. Ashmita is the queen of this demon king, and they are both the parents of the demon king Mahishasura. This story is part of the Puranic literature, which was composed between 400 BCE and 400 CE.

Another reference to the name Ashmit is found in the 16th century Indian epic poem 'Ramayana'. In this text, Ashmit is the name given to King Vibhishana, who was the younger brother of the demon king Ravana. King Vibhishana defected from his brother's side and joined the side of Lord Rama, the hero of the epic. The name Ashmit was given to him as a mark of his penance and atonement for his past demonic deeds.
